name: Neo-Nazism
summary: Neo-Nazism is the post-1945 revival of Nazi ideas: the supremacy of a white or Aryan race, central hostility to Jews, rejection of liberal democracy in favor of a leader-led racial state, and admiration for Hitler and the Third Reich. Its movements range from Rockwell-style street parties and white-power subcultures to esoteric, pagan and National Bolshevik currents. Holocaust denial, replacement conspiracy theories and ethnostate aims are common, and some groups have turned to paramilitary violence.
scope: Mainstream post-war neo-Nazism as shown in the 1920 NSDAP 25-point program the movement draws on, George Lincoln Rockwell's American Nazi Party and World Union of National Socialists, David Lane's Fourteen Words, and the groups surveyed in the Wikipedia article (National Socialist Movement, Combat 18, Blood & Honour and European parties). It excludes the historical Nazi regime as such, which is covered by national-socialism, and treats esoteric (Serrano, Evola) and National Bolshevik strands as minority variants. Economic positions are mostly inferred because neo-Nazi groups give them little attention.

sources.usedFor: Rockwell's views on Jews, race, repatriation, Holocaust denial, homosexuality and violence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 25 Points call for expanded pensions and protection of mothers and infants, so state care for the racial community fits, though universal healthcare for all residents is never stated.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Neo-Nazi sources stress jobs for citizens and attack "interest slavery" but say little about wage floors; adherents split between a nationalist-socialist and a pro-business reading.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Point 10 puts the common good above individual interest and Point 13 nationalizes trusts, so unfettered markets are distrusted, though the stance is inferred from a 1920 program.

public-ownership.rationale: Point 13 nationalizes trusts, but Rockwell's WUNS began as "Free Enterprise" National Socialists and the Strasserist and business-friendly strands disagree.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The program targets unearned income and war profits rather than wealth as such, and modern neo-Nazis are divided on class issues, so no clear position emerges.

unions-good.rationale: Neo-Nazi movements mostly ignore labor unions or treat them as Marxist and Jewish-influenced, with only the Strasserist current favoring workers' organizations; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Point 17 allows expropriation without compensation for public use, while Rockwell-style groups defended private enterprise; adherents are split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Points 12, 13 and 14 impose profit-sharing and nationalization on large firms, suggesting regulation of corporations, but modern groups rarely discuss it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare for the racial community is accepted (Points 7 and 15) while welfare for outsiders is rejected, so a general cut is not a clear position.

worker-ownership.rationale: The program favors profit-sharing, not worker ownership, and neo-Nazis oppose Marxist collectivism; the answer is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Neo-Nazis want a strong security state against "subversives", yet distrust the existing government and many fear its surveillance of them; inferred and contested.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Neo-Nazi movements portray drugs as racial degeneration and stress discipline, so legalization is unlikely to be favored, though libertarian-leaning strands exist.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Neo-Nazis are the usual targets of hate-speech and Holocaust-denial laws (for example in Germany) and oppose them as censorship of their views.

strong-leader.rationale: Neo-Nazism inherits the Fuhrer principle; the article describes groups that aim to set up a fascist state and revere Hitler as "the greatest leader of all time".

state-harmful.rationale: Neo-Nazism seeks a strong racial state (Point 25 demands strong central power), the opposite of the view that the state is unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Armed paramilitary groups such as Combat 18 and The Order show a preference for arms in white hands, although a racial state would restrict them for others; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Point 22 calls for a national army and the movement glorifies military order and discipline, favoring strong security forces under a racial state.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The program stresses public morality and prosecutes art that harms national life (Point 23), so legal sex work is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Point 25 demands a strong central power over the whole Reich and rejects federal particularism.

rehabilitation.rationale: Point 18 demands the death penalty for criminals who harm the nation, and the movement favors harsh punishment over reform.

traditional-family.rationale: The Fourteen Words tie survival of the race to white children and the "White Aryan woman", making the traditional family the vehicle of racial continuity.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Rockwell is reported to have hated gay people and planned to jail them, and the Nazi inheritance includes homophobia, so recognizing same-sex marriage is rejected.

abortion-legal.rationale: Concern for white birth rates and "white genocide" makes neo-Nazis oppose abortion among whites, though some favor it for other groups; the main line is opposition.

more-religion-public.rationale: Neo-Nazis are split among agnostics, Christian Identity, Odinists, pagans and occultists, so there is no common view on religion in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Rockwell blamed Jews for civil rights agitation and wanted Black Americans repatriated; neo-Nazis reject programs for racial redress as anti-white.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The racial-biological worldview treats sex roles as natural and fixed, as in the Fourteen Words' stress on the "White Aryan woman" as mother.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The 1920 program ties the nation to German blood and culture (Points 4 and 23), and modern neo-Nazi groups hold events around heritage figures, so defending national culture is central.

gradual-change.rationale: Neo-Nazis seek to overthrow liberal democracy, in some cases through paramilitary plans, rather than reform within established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Point 8 demands a halt to all non-German immigration and expulsion of recent arrivals, a position later neo-Nazi parties repeat as anti-immigration politics.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Lane saw the US as a vehicle for a "global Zionist government"; neo-Nazis treat international bodies like the UN as Jewish-dominated and reject them.

free-trade.rationale: The program's priority is national self-sufficiency and attacks on "Jewish-materialist" finance, implying hostility to globalized free trade; stated only indirectly.

nation-first.rationale: Point 10 subordinates individual interest to the nation and the whole program puts the Volk and its interests first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject universal human rights and oppose interventions as serving Jewish or globalist interests.

open-borders.rationale: Point 5 and 8 confine non-citizens to guest status and end immigration, directly opposing open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits on growth are not a core neo-Nazi theme, though "blood and soil" and some esoteric strands value nature; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is rarely addressed and is usually dismissed as globalist, though ecofascist strands exist; low-confidence inference.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Neo-Nazis are split between technological modernism and anti-modern mystical strands such as Evola and Serrano's Hyperborean doctrine.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No documented common position; adherents have no stated stance on nuclear energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement seeks to replace liberal democracy with a fascist state and some groups have planned paramilitary attacks, so revolutionary change is accepted.

experts-over-public.rationale: Elite rule by the racially worthy is favored but neo-Nazis distrust academia and experts as hostile, so the answer is split.

central-planning.rationale: Points 13 and 17 point to state control of some sectors, but the movement offers no worked planning doctrine and strands differ.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public or worker ownership of firms is not a goal beyond Point 13's trusts; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Point 17 bans land speculation, but a land-value tax is never mentioned.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Neo-Nazis favor family continuity and the program does not attack inheritance as such; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Point 10 makes work a duty of every citizen, which contradicts an unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The program's nationalism and Point 7 prioritize domestic jobs; neo-Nazis generally back protection of national industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Points 13 and 14 give the state a role over large firms, and a strong racial state would steer the economy; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Point 16 favors small business and land reform for the common people against large capital and department stores.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Point 10 makes work a duty and Point 11 ends unearned income only; the program keeps wages and rejects Marxist abolition of money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Point 11's "breaking of interest slavery" suggests hostility to banking power, but abolishing central banks is not explicit.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Point 25 proposes occupational chambers, which links to state-recognized corporatist bodies, though modern neo-Nazis seldom elaborate it.

one-party-rule.rationale: The article says neo-Nazi movements aim to establish a fascist state, and the DSSS was dissolved for seeking a "National Socialist system".

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The program points to a strong leader and national parliament rather than a monarch, though some strands (for example Serbian Action) favor an Orthodox monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The article states neo-Nazism rejects liberal democracy, and a Czech court found a party sought to replace democracy with a National Socialist system.

direct-votes.rationale: Point 25 calls for a central parliament under a strong state; plebiscitary democracy is not part of the program.

workers-councils.rationale: Rejects Marxist council rule; Point 25 gives power to a central state with occupational chambers.

right-to-secede.rationale: The program demands a unified Greater Germany and strong central power, so secession is rejected, except where a white homeland breakaway is sought (Lane).

natural-rulers.rationale: The hierarchy of races and the leader principle assume that some peoples and individuals are born to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Combat 18, the NSU, The Order and others used violence and Rockwell's White Power called for killing enemies, so violence is not ruled out.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nazi doctrine glorified struggle and soldierly virtue, and neo-Nazis revere the Wehrmacht tradition; inferred from the movement's militarism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Point 24 conditions religious freedom on service to the nation's moral sense, and Christian Identity and pagan strands want religion tied to race; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian Identity members hold scripture-based views but most neo-Nazis follow racial doctrine rather than scripture; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement wants a strong state monopoly on force and law (Points 19 and 25).

military-superiority.rationale: Point 22 and the revival of a national army show a taste for military strength and Greater Germany.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Lane's Fourteen Words aim to secure the existence of a white people and seek a white homeland, while the NSM seeks a "white ethnostate"; Point 4 limits citizenship to those of German blood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Point 9 and 10 and the national community ideal explicitly replace class conflict with national unity.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy of races and individuals is central; the program asks equal rights only among citizens of the right blood.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Neo-Nazis claim lands for their own racial nation (blood and soil) and do not support non-white indigenous authority; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Rejecting guilt and redress claims by non-white nations is consistent with their racial worldview and Holocaust-denial revisionism.

civilizational-union.rationale: The pan-European and "White Europe" currents, as in Yockey's pan-European neo-Nazism and Polish "White Europe" banners, seek racial union across borders.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Point 10 says individual interest must be subordinate to the common good, the opposite of treating self-interest as a moral virtue.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Point 10 subordinates individual interest to the community and requires work as a civic duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Esoteric and pagan strands venerate nature while others are indifferent; no common stance.

limit-population.rationale: The Fourteen Words and replacement theory call for more white births, so population limits are opposed for whites; for others some would favor them.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Evola and Serrano-style strands are anti-modern, but most neo-Nazis admire Nazi industrial and military achievement; split and inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Neo-Nazi strands range from modernist admirers of Nazi technology to anti-modern mystics, and no shared position on disruptive technology appears in the sources.

human-enhancement.rationale: Racial purity and natural hierarchy outlook is hostile to open-ended transhumanism, though eugenic enhancement of the race might be welcomed; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule is meant to rest with a human leader and racial elite, not algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Neo-Nazis want to evade surveillance but support a strong security state for themselves; no clear position.

restore-past-order.rationale: Neo-Nazis seek revival of a lost racial order, such as the Third Reich or a Fourth Reich, though they also claim a revolutionary rebirth.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is dogmatically ideological about race and Hitler, so judging policy by results rather than doctrine is rejected.

direct-action.rationale: Street activism, rallies and paramilitary plans (NSM riots, Combat 18) show a preference for action beyond elections, though some parties contest elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Violence, intimidation and authoritarian organization are used to build a racial state, so means do not mirror the aim of a harmonious society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in neo-Nazi sources suggests a return to hunter-gathering, and the movement admires industrial and military power, so strong disagreement is inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The program keeps labor, class chambers and a middle class (Points 16 and 25) with no abolition of specialization.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Point 10 makes work a duty and Point 11 bans unearned income, so reward follows contribution to the nation rather than need.

production-for-use.rationale: Point 11 ends interest slavery and Point 12 targets war profits, but the program keeps profit as such (Point 14 shares it).

profit-exploitation.rationale: The program attacks "unearned" and speculative profit as Jewish, not the Marxist theory that all business profit is exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Neo-Nazis treat communism as an enemy, naming communists among those to be fought, so class dictatorship over former rulers is firmly rejected.

collective-farming.rationale: Point 17 land reform aims at small owners, not collective farms; communism is rejected.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Neo-Nazi texts blame Jewish finance for wars rather than capitalism as a system; mapping is inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Point 10 and 25 accept a strong state with obligations to the community.

harm-principle.rationale: The state would restrict adults on grounds of racial and moral health, such as imprisoning gay people (Rockwell), beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are tied to blood and citizenship (Points 4-6), not held by individuals as such.

conscription.rationale: Point 22 replaces the mercenary army with a national army, and the movement admires martial duty; neo-Nazis expect service by racial comrades.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Citizens are bound to the race and nation; neo-Nazis favor expelling others rather than exit as a check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Point 10 and 25 treat the state as the embodiment of the community, not a service provider.

positive-liberty.rationale: The program offers material provisions to the racial community but not as a theory of freedom; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Neo-Nazi circles promote "cultural Marxism" claims that media and academia are controlled by hostile elites, per the Wikipedia article.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The article defines neo-Nazism by racial supremacy, and Rockwell's White Power called Black people primitive; innate racial difference is a core claim.

organic-representation.rationale: Point 25's occupational chambers hint at functional representation; modern neo-Nazis seldom elaborate.

total-state.rationale: Point 25 builds a strong central state and Point 23 regulates press and culture, though modern groups also voice anti-state rhetoric.

national-rebirth.rationale: Neo-Nazi movements seek a rebirth of the white race and Aryan order, such as a Fourth Reich or White Europe.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Points 1 and 3 call for a Greater Germany and land for settlement; Lane sought a white homeland in the northwest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The leader principle and oaths to the Fuhrer suggest personal loyalty, but modern groups rarely use feudal language.

bound-labor.rationale: The program favors a duty to work, but land reform for small owners rather than bound serfs.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Neo-Nazis claim mainstream history and science are controlled by Jews (denial, "cultural Marxism"), consistent with seeing knowledge as shaped by power.

universal-morality.rationale: Racial hierarchy rejects universal moral truths; morality is tied to the race and its survival.

single-common-good.rationale: Point 10 places the common good above individual interests, in line with the picture of the Volk as one body with one interest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The article describes antisemitism as central, and groups hold anti-Israel demonstrations and want Jews eliminated or excluded from the nation.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Return of ethnic kin is welcome for whites but the idea has little documented discussion among neo-Nazis.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed by neo-Nazi sources; the program only restricts foreign-language newspapers (Point 23), which does not settle revival of a lost language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Authority runs from the leader downward; Point 10 and 14 give workers shares, not votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: The program expands state-run education under national control (Point 20); vouchers are not mentioned.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Neo-Nazi sources never discuss fiscal stimulus; the attack on "interest slavery" (Point 11) hints at hostility to debt but not a deficit rule.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rockwell's WUNS started as "Free Enterprise" National Socialists, but Point 10 subordinates economic liberty to the nation; mixed.

rule-by-example.rationale: Point 18 and the cult of strength favor punishment and force over example alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: Neo-Nazis claim self-determination for their own people, as in Point 1 and the Fourteen Words, but not as a universal right for all nations.

force-without-un.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject the UN as Jewish-dominated and favor force by national interest.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mysticism, Hyperborean myth and Wotanism play a role beside pseudo-scientific racism; mixed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Points 5-7 reserve jobs and rights for citizens of German blood and relegate others to guest status.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Point 10 requires every citizen to work and Point 11 ends unearned income.

class-collaboration.rationale: Point 9, 10 and 14 envisage national unity of employers and workers rather than class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: They glorify Europe's racial heritage and monuments (Hitler-birthday events, Hess banners), so sacrificing institutions is unlikely.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-American separatism (Lane) and National Bolshevik admiration for Stalin point toward anti-West fronts, while others are pro-White West; split.

workers-nation.rationale: Point 9, 10 and Point 4 organize workers as members of the national community of blood.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Fourteen Words' "White Aryan woman" and Nazi traditionalism assign women to maternal roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Point 11 of the 1920 program calls for breaking "interest slavery", which neo-Nazi groups carry on in their attacks on usury and finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Rockwell supported separation of races and repatriation of Black Americans, and the NSM aims at a white ethnostate, so law should classify and separate by race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rejects the Marxist theory of the state; the state embodies the nation's blood community.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No documented stance; right-wing populist affinity, low-confidence inference.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Point 4 and 5 deny citizenship to those not of German blood regardless of assimilation, so assimilation is rejected in favor of exclusion.

elite-replacement.rationale: The article lists "white genocide" and Great Replacement conspiracy theories as common neo-Nazi beliefs and Lane saw the US as committing genocide against whites.

proportional-representation.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject party-parliament democracy but some parties benefit from PR; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Rockwell's pan-white mission and Aryan universalism of Yockey and Serrano show missionary racial claims, but not exporting a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Fourteen Words and Nazi tradition affirm male-led gender order as natural, not oppressive.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Neo-Nazis attack the political class as Jewish-controlled or traitorous; Lane called loyalty to the US "racial treason".

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The article lists ableism as an inherited Nazi position, including eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Neo-Nazis glorify Nazi-era forces and deny crimes (Holocaust denial), so accountability for past killings is rejected.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Points 13, 16 and 17 give the state power over trusts, retail and land, and Point 25 builds a strong centre, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Fourteen Words say the beauty of the white Aryan woman must not perish from the earth, and Lane's "white children" aim opposes racial mixing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The article defines neo-Nazism as promoting supremacy of one's own racial group, and Rockwell called Jews "human parasites".

socialism-one-country.rationale: National Bolshevik strands admire Stalin but most neo-Nazis oppose socialism as Jewish.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Neo-Nazis claim white settler states for white people and reject the colonial framing, but no position on the question is documented.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Point 19 calls for a uniform German law, but religion-specific civil codes are not discussed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religion is not core to neo-Nazism and its adherents are divided among Christians, pagans and agnostics, so no common stance on conversion appears.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a neo-Nazi theme; no source addresses it, so mild disagreement is inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Point 24 supports "positive Christianity" without denomination while neo-Nazis are religiously divided.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist argument that neo-Nazi sources do not discuss; they want a strong state regardless, but not for this reason.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rejecting democracy and the leader principle means legitimacy comes from race and leadership, not consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism and protection of domestic industry favor export strength.

population-transfer.rationale: Rockwell proposed resettling Black Americans in a new African state, and the NSM's ethnostate would expel Jews, non-whites and LGBTQ people; Point 8 expels non-Germans.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rockwell's White Power called for killing non-white people, and the movement endorses violence against enemies.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist struggle between races underlies the ideology, and Point 10 stresses fighting for the nation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Neo-Nazi parties are themselves banned (DSSS), so they oppose it, but in power they would ban rivals; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not a concept in neo-Nazism; the hierarchical outlook is incompatible.

separated-powers.rationale: Point 25 demands strong central power with a centralized parliament, and the leader principle rejects checks between rival bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: Neo-Nazi parties and cadre groups see themselves as a racial elite leading the people, but it is not Leninist doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Priority goes to the racial community, including Point 15 pensions and Point 20 funding poor gifted children, not the poor as a class.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Point 10 and class collaboration favor no strikes against the national community, but unions are not discussed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Racial doctrine blames race and Jewish finance, not overpopulation; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The article describes xenophobia and white-nationalist aims, and the ethnostate goal rests on the claim that mixed populations are in conflict.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Point 6 limits office to citizens and rejects appointments for party loyalty only; leaders are chosen by leadership principle.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Strong-state outlook allows suspension of protections against enemies, as in the Nazi regime.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The program attacks profiteering (Point 12) which could justify price controls, but no neo-Nazi source addresses maximum prices and free-enterprise strands disagree; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Point 23 bans newspapers opposing national welfare and restricts foreign press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Neo-Nazis want a leader-led state with a national army (Point 22), but whether the army answers to the party or the state is not discussed; adherents are unlikely to have a settled view.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Point 4 and 5 bar non-Germans from citizenship, so long waits are less demanding than the norm.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not discussed; the program disfavors corrupt politicians but has no pay rule.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The leader principle and cadre discipline imply binding party decisions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Neo-Nazis oppose the EU and the "global Zionist government" frame, and champion national sovereignty; some pan-European strands want union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Under the leader principle the head of the movement or state commands the armed forces, as Hitler did, and neo-Nazi groups revere that model.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Neo-Nazis are not united on church organization, and the sources show no stance on how a national church should be governed.

clerical-rule.rationale: Neo-Nazism rejects rule by clergy in favor of racial-political leadership.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Neo-Nazi movements are nationalist and militarist, so they oppose defeatism in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Point 23 prosecutes art and literature that "disintegrate" national life.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A leader state with no electoral limit on the leader follows from the Fuhrer principle, which neo-Nazis celebrate, though the question is rarely posed directly.

recall-officials.rationale: Authority runs down from the leader, so voters recalling officials contradicts the leadership principle; inferred from the rejection of liberal democracy.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-American separatism supports withdrawal, while others favor white alliances; split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Point 17 land reform and Point 16 small business keep private markets; no ban on rent.

people-in-arms.rationale: Paramilitary groups and the white-power movement prize armed members, though Point 22 favors a national army; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The article cites a "blood and soil" ideal that values rural racial roots.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Point 1 demands union of all Germans, and neo-Nazi groups in Europe press for ethnic reunions.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Neo-Nazis scorn academia as ideologically controlled, per "cultural Marxism" claims.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The article defines neo-Nazism by supremacy of one's own racial group and Savitri Devi and Serrano's Aryan hierarchy; no culture or race is considered equal.

death-penalty.rationale: Point 18 demands the death penalty for usurers, profiteers and criminals harming the nation.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Neo-Nazis stress traditional gender roles and condemn LGBT recognition, so they would reject school teaching of gender equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Racial science claims modern evolution, though Christian Identity members hold creationism; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Point 23 prosecutes art and literature that harm national life; pornography is not named.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Point 4 of the program says only those of German blood can be citizens, a descent rule that neo-Nazi groups adopt for their own nations.

minority-language-support.rationale: Point 23 restricts foreign-language newspapers and Point 4 confines citizenship to the Volk.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Point 24 allows religious freedom only unless a creed offends the "Germanic race".

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Point 10 subordinates individuals to the community and the movement demands conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Opposes "interest slavery" but also rejects aid; no documented position.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A post-colonial question that neo-Nazi sources do not address; no stated position can be drawn from the program.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Neo-Nazis seek to impose a leader state, not an elected constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The movement has no documented economic-development theory, but Point 25's strong state suggests it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Neo-Nazis hold that white and non-white peoples are unequal and reject duties across races.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses nuclear weapons; the answer is inferred from the movement's militarism and distrust of foreign protectors.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The leader is not chosen by popular vote under the leadership principle, and neo-Nazis reject liberal democracy, so the answer is inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Point 11's attack on "interest slavery" suggests hostility to bankers' autonomy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Points 1 and 3 claim land for Germans and treat any surrender of territory as betrayal.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Point 10 subordinates individual interest to the common good and Point 17 allows expropriating land for public use without compensation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Neo-Nazis consider Soviet communism Jewish-run; some National Bolsheviks admire Stalin; no common view.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not a documented neo-Nazi theme, so no position can be inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Some neo-Nazis back white or Western alliances while anti-American strands (Lane, National Bolsheviks) reject them; adherents are split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Points 1 and 3 claim German land and settlement abroad, so the annexation ruling is not accepted.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Point 24 is positive toward Christianity without denomination but subordinates it to the Germanic race.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The leader principle makes the head the movement's own leader, as in the party-state model, not a symbol above politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Point 25's strong central power and territorial ambitions favor keeping the state whole.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Point 25 demands a centralized state authority over the whole Reich, leaving no room for a region with its own economic and legal system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Hitler is revered by neo-Nazis (the Hitler-birthday events) but divine descent is not claimed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Points 11-14 target unearned income and profit and imply progressive burdens.

character-from-environment.rationale: The article defines the ideology by racial supremacy, with inheritance of character, and Rockwell treated Black people as primitive by nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The leader principle and the aim of a fascist state place the leader's will above ordinary law, though neo-Nazi sources seldom state this in constitutional terms.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The program seeks a strong central leader-led state rather than a balance between the few and the many.

leader-cult.rationale: The article records Hitler's birthdays, praise as "the greatest leader of all time" and Rudolf Hess banners.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not a documented neo-Nazi topic; traditional-family views point to no clear answer.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Neo-Nazism rejects Marxism and class struggle outright, in favor of national unity of all classes.

land-redistribution.rationale: Point 17 expropriates land for public use without compensation and bans land speculation.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugees of non-white stock would not be admitted; return of co-ethnics is accepted.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Point 1 unites all Germans in a Greater Germany by self-determination, a claim modern neo-Nazi groups echo.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Nothing in neo-Nazi doctrine punishes leaving a religion, and members are religiously diverse, so the inference is mild disagreement.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a neo-Nazi theme, and Islam is seen as hostile; low-confidence inference.

common-currency.rationale: Neo-Nazis defend national sovereignty and distrust finance and the EU.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-European neo-Nazism (Yockey) and "White Europe" call for union of kindred peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Point 4 refuses nationality to minorities and Point 23 restricts minority press.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Neo-Nazis want minorities excluded or expelled (the NSM ethnostate, Rockwell's repatriation plan), not equal rights fought for in place.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Neo-Nazis hold that race and its struggle, not economic production, drive history, in contrast to Marxist materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Point 13 nationalizes trusts and Point 16 favors small business, but cartel bans are not stated.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed, but hostility to finance and "interest slavery" suggests little sympathy for rescuing banks; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Neo-Nazis favor the leader's will over both majorities and independent courts, so adherents would not sign a majoritarian-democratic claim.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Fourteen Words' vision of the white woman as mother and the movement's traditional roles reject quotas for equal female representation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Point 3 seeks land and colonies to feed the people, implying self-sufficient bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Neo-Nazis oppose international trade agreements as globalist and rarely discuss standards; the answer is inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Point 10 makes labor a civic duty for the common good, which aligns with moral incentives, but the point is not elaborated in neo-Nazi sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Lane and The Order sought to spark a revolution by insurrection and terror.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Racial hierarchy prizes lineage, and the Serbian neo-Nazi monarchy strand favors titles; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Point 20 aligns education with national life, and neo-Nazis want history taught from their own race and nation's centre.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: A racial hierarchy implies rule by superior peoples, but the sources do not frame it as a duty to improve subjects; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Point 20 teaches civics from an early age and the movement demands loyalty to the nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opponents of preferences for minorities, since they want white interests first; but not the colorblind principle.

public-money-creation.rationale: Point 11's attack on "interest slavery" aligns with public control of money.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Points 1 and 3 seek lost territories and colonies for Germany, but influence over former empire regions is not a stated neo-Nazi aim; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Neo-Nazis favor autarky for their own nation but say nothing on poor countries breaking ties with rich ones.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist concept that neo-Nazi sources do not address.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Neo-Nazis favor discrimination by right but also impose segregation by law; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Points 4 to 6 make rights depend on blood and citizenship, which a general bill of rights binding the government would contradict.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed by neo-Nazi sources; Point 2 voiding Versailles shows hostility to imposed treaties but not colonial ones.

elective-rulers.rationale: The leader principle replaces election with leadership, and neo-Nazis reject liberal democracy.

minority-veto.rationale: Point 10 puts the nation ahead of the individual, so a single dissenter cannot block a decision.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The leader principle gives the leader unquestioned authority; neo-Nazis revere Hitler as the greatest leader.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Point 25 vests authority in a strong central power and neo-Nazis seek to replace liberal parliamentary democracy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, so no position can be inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no position can be drawn.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duty runs to the racial community (Point 10, 15), but a general duty of the wealthy to the less fortunate is not stated; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement demands active service to the Volk, and neo-Nazis organize rallies and parties, so withdrawal is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Neo-Nazi circles blame Jewish-dominated media and "cultural Marxism" for decay, but not the Frankfurt-school claim of pacification; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim not addressed by neo-Nazi sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Neo-Nazis blame Jewish finance for exploitation, but not in this form.

native-born-offices.rationale: Point 6 limits public office to citizens, who under Point 4 must be of German blood.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties and does not apply to neo-Nazism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The program seeks self-sufficiency (Point 3) and attacks foreign finance, so reliance on one's own resources over foreign loans fits.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Point 2 voids the Versailles treaty and Point 1 unites all Germans in one state, so demanding lost lands is a stated aim.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Neo-Nazis want white rule in white-settled states, so they would reject indigenous leadership over settlers; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The neo-Nazi stance is revival of fascism and rejection of its condemnation (Holocaust denial).

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Neo-Nazis defend Nazi Germany and name communism as an enemy, rejecting any equation of the two.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Neo-Nazis in the US often back the Confederacy's racial order; no documented position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Neo-Nazis honour condemned figures, as the Hitler-birthday events and Hess banners show, so they would keep such monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not a stated neo-Nazi theme; anti-feminist leanings suggest mild agreement.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject liberal democracy as a universal model and favor an order based on race, so institutions are tied to peoples.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The movement's militarism and desire for a fascist state suggest a political role for armed forces, though it is rarely stated as a doctrine.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care of children is treated as a mother's natural duty to the race, so paying for it as labour is not a theme; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Family and racial continuity are central, so respect for parents is likely, though not discussed directly.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; neo-Nazi leadership rests on loyalty and race rather than examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Point 23 restricts foreign investment in the press, and nationalism extends it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The emphasis on the traditional family points toward restricting easy divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Authority flows down from the leader, so delegates bound by and removable by electors contradicts the leader principle.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Point 15 calls for expanding state old-age pensions, not replacing them with private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Point 17 expropriates land for public use and bans speculation, but small private ownership (Point 16) is also favored, so use-tenure is not a clear answer.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The leader principle and rejection of parliamentary democracy mean spending is not subject to elected approval; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Point 23 restricts foreign-language papers and the movement is nationalist.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Points 5 and 17 treat non-citizens as guests and restrict land speculation, so barring foreigners from owning land fits.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject anti-discrimination law and racial equality measures as anti-white.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Point 24 opposes the "Jewish-materialist spirit", which fits a critique of consumerism, though it is not elaborated.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be drawn.

corporate-influence.rationale: The program attacks trusts and Jewish finance (Points 13, 24) and neo-Nazis allege hidden control, so corporate influence is likely condemned, but it is not stated.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Point 23 restricts foreign investment in newspapers, a model neo-Nazis extend to protect the nation.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Fourteen Words seek more white children and replacement theory opposes immigration substituting for births.

residents-only-property.rationale: Points 5 and 17 favor citizens and land for the people, which fits local limits on purchases, but it is not stated.

job-guarantee.rationale: Point 7 obliges the state to provide a livelihood for citizens, with non-citizens expelled first if jobs run short.

democratic-peace.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject democracy and its promotion, and favor struggle among peoples over a peace based on democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The leader principle and demand for duty (Point 10) imply a duty to obey the leader, though neo-Nazis disobey the existing liberal state.

non-intervention.rationale: Some want non-intervention for isolationism; others want force; split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Unions are not a neo-Nazi theme and organizing form is not addressed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The article states Jews are central and casts conspiracy theories ("Jewish war", white genocide, "cultural Marxism") as common.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Fourteen Words and traditional-family views value legally recognized marriage within the race.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Press restrictions (Point 23) show a preference for controlling information, so a legal right of access is unlikely; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Autarky applies at the national level, and local production is not discussed.

informal-organisation.rationale: Neo-Nazis organize in parties and hierarchies, though leaderless resistance exists in parts of the movement; split with a slight lean against.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject international bodies as Jewish-dominated and put national interest first.

religious-nation.rationale: Neo-Nazis define the nation by race and blood, not religion, although Christian Identity and Orthodox strands link faith and nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject subordination, with national sovereignty central; ritual tribute is not discussed.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A centralized state (Point 25) controls revenue for the whole nation, so regions keeping their own is opposed; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Points 16 and 17 protect small property and neo-Nazis oppose communism and collective ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: Wikipedia lists anti-communism among enemies named (Bosnian group, Finnish bombers) and Rockwell portrayed civil rights as Jewish-communist.

religion-illusion.rationale: Neo-Nazism includes pagan, Christian and occult strands that treat religion as real, but few are Marxist materialists.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Point 24 and the attacks on finance treat capitalism as a Jewish-materialist force, not a progressive one.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject the premise of women's equality and uphold traditional roles.

socialized-care.rationale: Care is seen as the mother's role in the family for the race; public provision of childcare is not endorsed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Point 23 favors German-language press and restricts foreign-language papers, which fits linguistic purism, though not stated.

treaties-binding.rationale: Point 2 voids treaties imposed on Germany, and neo-Nazis seek to exclude minorities, so treaties with minorities are not honored; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject communism and collective property in favor of a centralized racial state.

majority-settlement.rationale: Point 3 seeks land for settlement and Lane sought a white homeland, so settling the ethnic majority in minority regions fits.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Neo-Nazis claim national socialism as a third way between "Jewish" capitalism and communism, a stance rooted in Point 14 and Point 24.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial is a common feature of neo-Nazism and Rockwell publicly denied that Jews were systematically murdered by the Nazis.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Rockwell said he would imprison gay people as an early priority in power, and homophobia is listed as an inherited Nazi position.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Blood-and-soil nationalism and the 25 Points' demand for land to sustain the racial community suggest a claim grounded in the race's tie to territory; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Neo-Nazism rejects liberal democracy for a leader-led racial state, which entails banning rival parties and organisations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The 25 Points allow religious freedom unless it endangers the race, and pagan and esoteric strands are hostile to church privilege; inferred, contested.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The 25 Points demand land and colonies to feed the people, implying territories run for the ruling nation's benefit; applied to modern movements by inference.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Most neo-Nazi groups are hostile to Muslims, though some admire Islamist anti-Zionism; inferred, outside the doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A Muslim doctrine of religious legitimacy is foreign to the movement; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The leader principle puts decisions in the hands of the Führer-style authority, not ordinary people's direct participation; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement's racial hierarchy and hostility to egalitarian frameworks make this a position it rejects; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Strongly hostile to LGBT rights and committed to fixed biological roles; inferred from the movement's general social positions.

assisted-dying.rationale: The Nazi regime's eugenic killings suggest sympathy, but modern groups give little attention to voluntary assisted dying; adherents are split or indifferent.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Neo-Nazis commonly present themselves as beyond left and right, and National Bolshevik currents explicitly merge them; inferred, contested.

alienated-labor.rationale: The claim is Marxist, and neo-Nazi programs inherit the 25 Points' stress on national, not class, labor and attack Marxism; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups treat non-white, Muslim immigrants as alien to a white homeland and oppose their settlement, as the Fourteen Words and the 25 Points' immigration clauses imply.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Neo-Nazism grounds authority in race and leader, with a pagan, esoteric or secular bent, though Christian Identity strands exist; inferred, so mild.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Neo-Nazism is hostile to Muslim and Jewish visibility but has no stated policy on it; adherents are split and this is inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment law is outside the doctrine and hostile to feminism and regulation conflicts with views on rights; adherents are split.

social-market-economy.rationale: The 25 Points favour state control over trusts and profit sharing against both liberal capitalism and Marxism, so a market-plus-welfare model is not matched; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The 25 Points call for a people's army and neo-Nazi groups glorify paramilitary force, so abolition is strongly opposed.

rich-first.rationale: The 25 Points call for abolishing unearned income and sharing profits, and nationalist solidarity is central, so unequal regional growth is not endorsed; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups are split between pro-Russian, anti-US and white-solidarity internationalist positions; the sources state no common line.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Nazi tradition rests on the Fuhrerprinzip chosen by merit and loyalty, not hereditary rule; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The 25 points demand breaking the bondage of interest, and neo-Nazi groups repeat it, but a user-owned bank model is inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Neo-Nazi rhetoric attacks international finance and the IMF as Jewish-led; inferred from the 25 points' stand against interest slavery.

property-franchise.rationale: The 25 points tie the vote to citizenship by blood, not property, so a property test is not their criterion.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Neo-Nazism affirms rigid gender roles and a blood-and-soil view of nature; the statement's feminist-ecological premise is opposed.

reification.rationale: Neo-Nazis blame finance capital and Jews rather than capitalism's structure; they reject Marxist analysis, but the answer is inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Point 23 of the 25 points demands that the press be controlled by Germans and attacks the Jewish-owned press, and neo-Nazis say media is owned by the rich and Jews.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Fuhrerprinzip puts the leader's will above standing law, and neo-Nazi groups reject liberal legal constraints on rulers.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 25 points limit citizenship, and therefore voting and office, to those of German blood, and Rockwell's program applies it to whites.

online-participation.rationale: Neo-Nazis use the internet heavily but reject democratic deliberation; the doctrine does not address it, so inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Neo-Nazism favours leader-driven rule over public accountability; inferred, with no stated position.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The sources restrict marriage by race, not religion; Christian-identity and pagan strands differ, so adherents are split and this is inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotting Jewish shops echoes the Nazi 1933 boycott and the 25 points' attack on Jewish commerce, and neo-Nazi groups still campaign for it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Neo-Nazism rejects democracy and deliberation by random citizens in favour of authoritarian leadership.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups include Christian-identity, pagan and atheist strands with no common stance; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The 25 Points demand breaking the bondage of interest and confiscating war profits, so concentrated finance is treated as a threat, though framed in racial terms.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the movement's cult of martial racial virility and traditional norms; the opened sources do not discuss military service by gay people.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Point 24 of the program endorses 'positive Christianity' and the state is not atheist, though pagan strands reject Christianity too.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The program demands ruthless action against criminals and a strong authoritarian state, the opposite of abolishing police and prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Neo-Nazism rejects liberal democracy for a leader-led racial state and limits citizenship to the racial community, so sharing power among communities is refused.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The 25 Points favour state pensions and welfare for the racial community, so private charity is not preferred; inferred, as the sources say little on this.

term-limits.rationale: A leader-led state under the leader principle has no place for electoral term limits on rulers.

vote-delegation.rationale: Rejection of liberal democracy and the leader principle make citizen vote delegation foreign to the ideology.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Neo-Nazi concern centres on racial survival ('white genocide' claims, Fourteen Words) rather than human extinction; adherents have no documented position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditional gender roles and mostly male-led hierarchies; religious offices are not addressed in the sources.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditional, male-led family ideal; marital authority is not explicitly discussed in the opened sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The 25 Points limit citizenship to people of German blood and put non-citizens under foreigner laws.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed by neo-Nazi sources; inferred only from the 25 Points' general land-reform language.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the 25 Points' aim to protect productive national enterprise; no stated position on patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups model themselves on the Hitler Youth and organise drilled, uniformed youth sections.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from militarist, strength-oriented outlook.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from hostility to foreign influence ('ZOG') and the demand for national sovereignty.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Neo-Nazism is marked by Holocaust denial and rejects official recognition of mass killings of Jews.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The 25 Points demand abolition of incomes unearned by work and 'breaking of interest slavery'.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Rockwell and the Fourteen Words milieu accept violence in defence of the race.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the racial-descent view of nations, which stresses continuity of blood rather than of state.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Neo-Nazi ideology rests on biological determinism of sex and race.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Neo-Nazism assigns fixed biological roles to women as racial mothers.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups honour their dead as martyrs, a cult inherited from the Nazi movement.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Rockwell framed politics as a racial struggle with near-religious intensity; esoteric strands go further. Inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Fourteen Words aim to secure territory and existence for the white race, not a cultural centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's priority on seizing state power for the racial state.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from Christian Identity-style and pagan strands, which are masculine in outlook.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of feminism and equality.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The 25 Points attack Jewish economic influence and demand that the economy serve the racial community.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The first of the 25 Points demands union of all Germans in a Greater Germany.

independent-unions.rationale: The Nazi programme the movement draws on put labour under a single state-led structure, so independent unions are inferred to be unwelcome.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The 25 Points ground the state in race and nation, not class power; neo-Nazi National Bolshevik strands are a minority, so mild disagreement is inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The 25 Points call for nationalising trusts and communalising department stores, so public control of essentials fits, though local services are not named.

second-chamber.rationale: The programme demands a strong central authority and the movement rejects liberal parliamentary checks, so a second chamber is inferred to be disfavoured.

municipal-property.rationale: The programme demands a strong central state and nationalisation rather than community ownership, so mild disagreement is inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Point 25 of the 1920 programme calls for unconditional central authority over the whole Reich, which opposes confederal rule by local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: The 25 Points stress protecting mothers and the racial community's families, so support for a wage that sustains a family is inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not addressed by neo-Nazi sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; a state-centred ideology is hostile to untraceable money, while groups in practice value privacy, so no position emerges.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed as a principle; groups in practice use anonymity for protection, but the ideology does not endorse it as a right.

person-over-state.rationale: Point 24 of the NSDAP programme puts the common interest before self-interest, and the movement's racial state subordinates the individual to the people.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Esoteric and pagan strands affirm spiritual nature while others are materialist and racial, so the movement is split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Point 25 asks for a strong central authority over the whole state, so regional powers resting on central permission fit, though regions are not discussed.

gm-crops.rationale: Its blood-and-soil, rural and nature-romantic strand makes genetic engineering of food suspect, though it is not addressed directly.

dense-cities.rationale: Blood-and-soil rural ideals and hostility to cosmopolitan cities suggest mild disagreement, inferred rather than stated.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Fourteen Words and the movement's racial-nationalist core hold that the white race has interests it must defend, so organising by race is central.

racial-pride.rationale: White pride and white power are central to the movement, and the Fourteen Words treat the race's survival as the highest duty.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The 25 Points demand land and territory for the German people and the movement admires the Reich's conquests, so limiting force to defence is rejected.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The 25 Points open by demanding the union of all Germans in a Greater Germany across state borders, which this movement inherits, though it grounds the nation in race rather than language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from rejection of liberal pluralism in favour of a single racial state; separate electorates for religious communities are not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Neo-Nazi movements commonly claim hidden Jewish or global forces are undermining and replacing the white nation, a conspiratorial framing that fits this statement though not worded as partition.

free-public-college.rationale: The 25 Points ask for state-funded education of gifted poor children but nothing on general free tuition, and modern groups give little attention to it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups give little attention to pollution taxes, and esoteric or blood-and-soil strands favour the environment while others ignore it.

future-generations.rationale: The Fourteen Words stress securing a future for white children, and blood-and-soil strands value the land, but this is about the race rather than the Earth generally.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The movement exalts motherhood and traditional roles but prizes martial hardness over care and nonviolence, so weighting those values more is not its aim.

arms-reduction.rationale: The movement admires the Third Reich's militarism, glorifies paramilitary struggle, and Rockwell's party was organised on military lines, so disarmament is rejected.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the leader-led, authoritarian state model and conspiratorial outlook, which favour discretion in foreign affairs.

capital-controls.rationale: The 25 Points demand breaking the bondage of interest and nationalising trusts, and inferring from this, adherents favour state control over finance.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups style themselves as paramilitary and street forces and reject the legitimacy of the existing state, so they refuse a state monopoly on arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to wars it sees as fought for Jewish interests, though it glorifies martial duty to the race; adherents split.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The 25 Points aim at a national economy serving the racial community and the Nazi regime abolished independent unions; neo-Nazi groups rarely back union bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the 25 Points' emphasis on national self-reliance and breaking 'interest slavery' rather than state top-ups; not stated in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Neo-Nazi sources say little about borrowing limits beyond attacks on 'interest slavery'; adherents split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Neo-Nazis reject international aid and global institutions as Jewish-controlled, so a rules reform for poorer countries is opposed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of the existing system as hostile to the white race and its goal of a new leader-led racial state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The movement wants one agreed racial-national order set by a leader, not a plurality of economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the blood-and-soil strand of Nazi thought, which treats nature as the homeland of the race, not as an asset to be priced.

sacred-nation.rationale: The racial community, the Volk, is the central object of devotion in neo-Nazism, as the Fourteen Words make the survival of the white race the highest purpose.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the movement's view that welfare should serve the racial community; graduates' debt relief is not discussed in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the movement's ethnic-nationalist view that the nation is a racial unit; the framing of rich regions exploiting poor ones is not used.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Neo-Nazism holds that humans are divided into unequal races and that dignity belongs to the racial community, and it favours eugenic redesign, so a universal human nature is rejected.

public-service-media.rationale: The 25 Points call for the press to serve the national interest, and neo-Nazis want media under racial-nationalist control, so independent public media is opposed.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Neo-Nazism centres on racial particularism and hierarchy, which sits badly with a universal spiritual truth shared by all faiths, though esoteric strands differ; inferred from the racial doctrine.

farm-price-support.rationale: The 25 Points call for land reform and protection of the peasantry within a racial state; farm price support is not stated, so this is inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups are militarist and hostile to disarmament by their own state; no source states a nuclear position, so this is inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: A leader-led racial party is the model, and class-based or independent workers' parties are rejected in favour of the racial community; inferred from the leader-state aim.

ban-fgm.rationale: Neo-Nazis are hostile to imported minority practices and would back a ban as a foreign custom; the sources never discuss FGM, so this is inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Nazi-derived doctrine stresses traditional gender roles but the 25 Points do not address women's property; adherents are not clearly split or clearly aligned, so this is left neutral.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language naming is not an issue the neo-Nazi sources address, and pan-German and nationalist strands would answer differently.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The 25 Points put the common good before individual good and favour a strong state, so private-law liability in place of state control is unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The model is a leader-led racial state with no place for customary chiefs in lawmaking; inferred from that model.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Blood-and-soil themes and the 25 Points' common good before individual good point to subordinating liberty, though environmental priority is not a stated aim.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The 25 Points demand ruthless action against criminals and the heaviest penalties, which fits fixed statutory sentences over judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Neo-Nazis want immigrants removed or excluded and reject assimilation of other races, so a language requirement misses their aim; inferred from the racial doctrine.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The 25 Points do not address union membership and neo-Nazi groups give labor little attention; inferred as split between anti-union and corporatist strands.

voter-id.rationale: Neo-Nazis favor restricting the vote to the racial community, so strict citizenship tests fit; the sources never discuss ID rules.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Not addressed directly; strands differ between Christian Identity, pagan and secular, so no single answer fits.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Neo-Nazism rejects liberal democracy in favor of a leader-led racial state and would not call a government democratic merely for holding elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the Fourteen Words and the focus on racial reproduction within families, though subcultures are permissive.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; movements rely heavily on the internet yet favor an authoritarian state, so adherents would split by who holds power.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The 25 Points call for abolishing unearned income and expanding state provision for the racial community, which does not fit replacing welfare with a cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 25 Points are silent on the question, but neo-Nazis favor a leader-led state and traditional roles for women; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not a neo-Nazi concern; inferred from their traditional gender roles and hostility to feminism.

race-social-construct.rationale: Neo-Nazism holds that biological races exist and differ in worth, which the Fourteen Words and Rockwell's writings state forcefully.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from hostility to feminism and state-promoted equality as seen in the movement's traditional gender ideology.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the NSDAP programme's land reform and subordination of private interest to the national good; first-claim ownership is not stated.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Holocaust denial and hostility to the post-war order, which treats Nuremberg-style trials as illegitimate.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the NSDAP programme backs only a 'positive Christianity' and many neo-Nazi strands are pagan or esoteric, so literal inerrancy is not typical.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the movement's racial-nationalist and traditional family emphasis, which does not prize gender equality; no source addresses self-government rules.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-communism and hostility to Marxism, which Rockwell stressed; no source addresses defending a planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects liberal democracy for leader-led rule, which is appointment from above rather than delegates chosen by lower councils.

national-church-status.rationale: The NSDAP programme grants freedom to denominations that do not threaten the state rather than a legal privilege for one church; the movement is also partly pagan.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Citizenship by blood and the aim of a white ethnostate leave no room for autonomous minority regions inside the state.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the leader-led racial state and ethnostate aims, which put race and the leadership above local votes; no source addresses plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the white-homeland aim, which calls for redrawing borders along racial lines; no source addresses colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Some strands praise blood-and-soil rural life but the programme and groups give no common ideal of limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the movement's ethnic-separatist view that peoples should hold their own homelands free of outside settlement; not stated for indigenous peoples specifically.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the NSDAP programme's people's army and the movement's traditional gender roles, which make women's drafting unlikely; no source states it.

missingStatements.text: The Holocaust did not happen as historians describe it.
missingStatements.rationale: Holocaust denial is a common feature of neo-Nazism and Rockwell publicly denied that Jews were systematically murdered by the Nazis.

missingStatements.text: Adolf Hitler was a great leader whose legacy deserves admiration.
missingStatements.rationale: Neo-Nazi groups hold Hitler-birthday events, call him the greatest leader of all time, and use 88 as shorthand for Heil Hitler.
missingStatements.declined: Admiration of one named person only separates this ideology from the rest; leader-cult already covers honoring a leader.

missingStatements.text: Sexual relations between adults of the same sex should be a criminal offence.
missingStatements.rationale: Rockwell said he would imprison gay people as an early priority in power, and homophobia is listed as an inherited Nazi position.

notes: Strands differ: Strasserist and National Bolshevik currents lean economically left and anti-American, Rockwell-era groups were pro-free-enterprise at the start, and esoteric currents are mystical rather than materialist. Many economic and technology answers are low-confidence inferences.
